method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18, the 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 rulings on negatives, and the writing-l4-rules skill; focus: the Act as host of the National Law (its own ss 1-10 and the Part 4 modifications that make Queensland a co-regulatory jurisdiction), with the National Law (Queensland) provisions a complainant meets. The two duties stated in days for the complainant's matter (s 150(1) 60 days, s 192(2)(b) 30 days) are regulative rules (PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN ... HENCE FULFILLED LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) and the seat questions read plain dates; no REFUSE (gaps answer `not covered`, asserted); every judgment of a Board, panel, the health ombudsman or a court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Health Practitioner Regulation National Law Act 2009 (Qld), in force from 2026-04-10, and the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law (Queensland) as published by Queensland Legislation, in force from 2026-04-10, both retrieved 2026-11-06 and deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2009-045.txt and act-2009-hprnlq.txt (plain-text conversions of the HTML view, not the authorised PDFs). Where the Act's Part 4 text and the published Law (Queensland) differ (s 151), the published Law was encoded (NOTES.md finding 3). Registration standards and national regulations not deposited; none sets a number used. The Health Ombudsman Act 2013 is deposited beside this subject but not encoded; it is named in the answers.

checks.command: l4 run hprnlq-dates.l4 ; l4 run hprnlq-complainant.l4 ; l4 run hprnlq-cases-complainant.l4
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the two regulative rules are asserted through CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED.

scope: The Act: ss 3-7C, 9, and Part 4 as it bears on the provisions below (in particular ss 15, 21-30, 32-34, 35A, 37, 37A, 40A, 42, 46-50, 56AA, 59). The National Law (Queensland): s 5 (definitions used); s 129; Part 8 ss 138, 139A-139C; Div 2 ss 139D, 140, 141, 141A-141C, 142(1), (2); Div 3 ss 143A, 144, 145; Div 4 s 146; Div 5 ss 148, 149, 150(1), 151(1)-(4); ss 159A, 161(3)(b), (4), 167A, 177A, 180(1)(b), (2), 187, 189, 192(2)(b), (4); Div 12 Subdiv 1 ss 193, 193A(1), 193B(2)-(4), 193C(1); s 237; Sch 7 cl 12 (business day, weekends only), cl 31(2), (3). Out: the Act ss 1, 2, 8, 9A, 10 and the rest of Part 4 (fees, Board procedure, interim prohibition orders, registers, offences, Part 12A transitional, s 328); the Law's Parts 1-7 otherwise, s 130, s 143 and the student limbs of Div 2, ss 150(2)-150C, 151(1A), Divs 6-14 otherwise, Parts 9-12 otherwise; the Health Ombudsman Act 2013 (each item and why in NOTES.md, Scope).
seat: the complainant: usually a patient, or a patient's family member, harmed by or worried about a registered health practitioner's care or conduct in Queensland, who may also be bringing or settling a negligence claim
